title: How stationary waves form practice mark scheme

questions.answer: When waves overlap, the resultant displacement is the sum of the individual displacements.

marking_points.text: States that overlapping wave displacements are added algebraically to give the resultant displacement

option_feedback.A: The waves must travel oppositely and remain matched.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Same-type waves of equal frequency and amplitude travelling oppositely and overlapping can form a stationary wave.
option_feedback.C: Same-direction waves do not produce the required fixed pattern.
option_feedback.D: The waves must be the same type and frequency.

marking_points.text: Selects B, same-type equal-frequency equal-amplitude waves travelling oppositely and overlapping

option_feedback.A: Zero displacement at one instant is not enough to establish zero amplitude.
option_feedback.B: An antinode can pass through zero displacement.
option_feedback.C: Correct. A node has zero amplitude through time.

marking_points.text: Selects C, requiring zero amplitude through time before identifying a node

option_feedback.A: An antinode can have zero instantaneous displacement.
option_feedback.C: An antinode is a fixed position, not a travelling crest.
option_feedback.D: Correct. Its oscillation amplitude is maximum.

marking_points.text: Selects D, a fixed position where oscillation amplitude is maximum

parts.answer: The reflected wave travels in the opposite direction to the incident wave.

marking_points.text: States that the reflected wave travels opposite to the incident wave

parts.answer: The incident and reflected waves are the same type with equal frequency and equal amplitude, travel oppositely and overlap. Their continuous superposition produces fixed nodes and antinodes, forming a stationary wave.

marking_points.text: States that the same-type waves have equal frequency and equal amplitude and travel in opposite directions
States that the two waves overlap and superpose
Links repeated superposition to a stationary pattern with fixed nodes and antinodes

parts.answer: Nodes: P, R and T. Antinodes: Q and S.

marking_points.text: Identifies P and R as nodes
Identifies Q and S as antinodes

parts.answer: A chosen node remains at equilibrium in every snapshot, so its amplitude is zero. A chosen antinode reaches the greatest displacement on opposite sides of equilibrium, so its amplitude is maximum.

marking_points.text: Explains that the chosen node remains at equilibrium in every snapshot and has zero amplitude
Explains that the chosen antinode reaches maximum displacement on both sides of equilibrium

parts.answer: At t1: A = 0 mm, B = +6 mm, C = 0 mm. At t2: A = 0 mm, B = -6 mm, C = 0 mm.

marking_points.text: Gives A = 0 mm at both instants
Gives B = +6 mm at t1 and -6 mm at t2
Gives C = 0 mm at both instants

parts.answer: A and C are nodes because their resultant is zero at both opposite extreme configurations of the complete cycle. B is an antinode because its resultant reaches the largest opposite extreme values, +6 mm and -6 mm.

marking_points.text: Identifies A and C as nodes and B as an antinode
Explains both nodes using zero resultant at both opposite extreme configurations
Explains the antinode using maximum reinforcement and opposite extreme resultants
